name: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
title: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
answer: Data loss prevention and sanitisation in AI covers the controls that keep sensitive data from leaving an organisation through prompts, outputs, training pipelines, retrieval stores, logs, and agent actions. It includes discovery and classification of personal data, trade secrets, source code, credentials, and regulated records, then the removal or alteration of that data before it reaches a model, a third party, or a user. Sanitisation here means redaction, masking, tokenisation, pseudonymisation, and synthetic replacement, not just deletion. The scope also takes in the evidence needed for an AI security audit, such as policy decisions, exceptions, and records of what was removed and why. It sits in enterprise enablement because teams need to use AI tools without turning every prompt into a data leak.

sections.body: Data loss prevention and sanitisation in AI covers the controls that keep sensitive data from leaving an organisation through prompts, outputs, training pipelines, retrieval stores, logs, and agent actions. It includes discovery and classification of personal data, trade secrets, source code, credentials, and regulated records, then the removal or alteration of that data before it reaches a model, a third party, or a user. Sanitisation here means redaction, masking, tokenisation, pseudonymisation, and synthetic replacement, not just deletion. The scope also takes in the evidence needed for an AI security audit, such as policy decisions, exceptions, and records of what was removed and why. It sits in enterprise enablement because teams need to use AI tools without turning every prompt into a data leak.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a mix of existing security stacks and AI-specific gateways. Endpoint agents, network egress filters, cloud access security brokers, email gateways, and API proxies inspect traffic for sensitive patterns. Data catalogues and classification engines tag stores, while tokenisation vaults, key managers, and secrets managers hold the replacements and keys. For AI systems, model gateways, prompt firewalls, vector database access controls, and logging pipelines apply policy at the point of inference and retrieval. Audit trails, SIEM platforms, and evidence stores keep the records that auditors and counsel later review.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners start with data discovery and classification, using pattern matching, exact data matching, fingerprinting, and machine learning classifiers to find sensitive content. Policy is then expressed as rules for what may leave, what must be redacted, and what requires an exception. Sanitisation techniques include redaction, masking, tokenisation, format-preserving encryption, pseudonymisation, and synthetic data generation, with checks for re-identification risk. For AI, the method adds prompt and output filtering, retrieval filtering, canary tokens, and watermarking, plus red team tests that try to extract training data or bypass filters. Each step produces evidence, such as classification reports, policy versions, test results, and approval records, so the audit can be reconstructed.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The legal side covers privacy, confidentiality, intellectual property, contractual duties, data subject rights, cross-border transfers, retention, and deletion. Provenance matters because training data, fine-tuning data, and retrieval content need a documented origin, licence, and consent basis, and because sanitisation must be defensible if a dispute arises. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, which shows how often data handling sits at the centre of AI disputes. Governance also covers employee monitoring, works council consultation, vendor risk, incident response, and breach notification. Auditors look for clear ownership, documented exceptions, and a chain of custody for sanitised data.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward AI-aware controls that understand context rather than matching fixed patterns. Expect more real-time guardrails for prompts, outputs, and agent tool calls, more use of confidential computing, federated learning, and synthetic data to avoid moving raw records, and more provenance standards for content and models. With 6979 state AI bills tracked on this site, compliance teams will face a patchwork of duties that DLP and sanitisation programmes must map to. Litigation over training data and trade secrets will keep pressure on organisations to show what data was used, what was removed, and who approved the removal. The practical result is that sanitisation records become as important as the sanitisation itself.
